chapter: Jamming, bootleg records and the Topsy hit
title: Financing 'Topsy' through the union and arranging it with Dick Hyman
summary: The money clears at the union, Dick Hyman arranges, and the Godfrey show band is hired for one number.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: know. (HUMMING) He says, okay. So I was talking to him and he talked very intelligent that night, this night, you know. I said well, I said, it's going to cost you XX amount of dollars for the arrangements. I said I've got to have the green light on the studio where we work. The engineers. And just every- things, so he says, okay, Cozy. I said we'll have to have our money deposited in the Union before we ever budge. Because I didn't know him, you know. So anyway Max Aaron was secretary then, he's the president of the union now. So I gave him the figure, this is what's going to happen, this would be done. Okay, Cozy. I thought that he was just jiving, so in a couple of days I called the Union and asked to speak to Max Aaron. Yeah. Well Max, is there a check up there for XX dollars for me? He said yeah, 'Cozy, give us another day or so so we can clear the check, I'll let you know.' Couple of days, I called, 'Yeah, Cozy, it's all cleared.' That's when I start saying, oh, this guy's for real. Came back in, well did you get your money. I said yeah, I says, now, I says now, we've got to get organized. Then's when I got together with Dick Hyman. He was the piano player during Arthur Godfrey's show, and so I had a studio then at 1697 Broadway. I said Dick, come on by, I said I've got a tempo and I've got just the thing, the beats that I want to put in this 'Topsy', I said we can get together a little arrangement. So he came by and we got together and we got the tempo all straight and Dick made the arrangement, and in the mean time I asked all the
guys in the band, in Arthur's band, did they want to make it? I never used my band, I used that band, Arthur Godfrey band, because all of them were expert readers.
Burt Farber was conducting, and so...

Piano, Yeah, but he was mostly in the control room, controlling everything. So I approached them all, I said to them, do you want to make this record. It was in the morning. And said all we got to do is one number, there's no three numbers for no record date, one number. I told them that too, I said all we're doing is one number. Now maybe I was spoiled a little bit, because I'd been used to doing those one-numbered sessions with Jackie Gleason and just one number and that's all, no three and four numbers during the whole session, everybody's tired, you know, and nobody wants to pay all them dues. So anyway. . . .
I think you want to ask me something about Frank Newton, didn't you?
